---
title: "Construction of GRS in TERRE and DIG-PD"
output: html_notebook
---

The manuscript "A Parkinson’s disease genetic risk score associates with blood DNAm on chromosome 17" explores how a genetic risk score (GRS) for Parkinson's disease (PD) associates with blood DNA methylation in the TERRE study of French agricultural workers, and evaluates GRS associations with DNAm in each sex as well as their sensitivity to non-genetic factors. This was originally spearheaded by Will Casazza and was posted as a pre-print on medRxiv in 2023. The current revision (2024, led by Sam Schaffner) aims to address previous reviewer feedback and prepare the manuscript for re-submission.

In this script, summary statistics from GP2 (Leonard et al., 2025) are used to construct GRS in TERRE and DIG-PD.

Created Sep 12, 2022 by Will Casazza

Updated Mar 19, 2026 by Samantha Schaffner: Final checks of GP2 SNPs present during DIG-PD QC stages.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(rcompanion)
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggpubr)
library(glue)
library(data.table)
library(IlluminaHumanMethylationEPICanno.ilm10b4.hg19)
library(biomaRt)
library(tidyr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

# PD risk score data and matching
```{r eval=FALSE}
# 157 independent loci reported in Leonard 2025 pre-print
gp2 <- read_xlsx("~/PD_GRS/suppl_GP2_2025.xlsx",sheet=4) %>%
  mutate(CHR = as.numeric(CHR), COUNTED = toupper(`Effect allele`), ALT = toupper(`Reference allele`), POS = BP) %>%
  filter(!is.na(CHR)) #90 SNPs
colnames(gp2)[2] <- "SNP"

snp_coord <- paste(paste("chr",pull(gp2[,4]),sep=""), pull(gp2[,5]), "SNP", sep=":")

#check goDMC SNP overlap
godmc <- read.csv("~/PD_GRS/coloc/godmc_assoc_meta_all_30Dec24.csv.gz")
nrow(godmc_sub <- godmc[godmc$snp %in% snp_coord,]) #11
write.csv(godmc_sub, file="~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/godmc_gp2_overlap.csv", row.names=F)
unique(godmc_sub$snp) #"chr8:109633256:SNP"
pull(gp2[gp2$CHR==8 & gp2$BP==109633256,"SNP"]) #"rs6469273"

gp2 %>%
  select(SNP, COUNTED, `Beta, all studies`) %>%
  write_delim("~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/gp2_2025_prs_file.txt", col_names = FALSE)
```

# TERRE PRS Analysis
Generate PRS using `plink2 --score`:
```{bash eval=FALSE}
~/plink2 --bfile ~/SHARE_DECIPHER/pd_grs_ewas_integration/TERRE_QC/raw_data.imputed.r2_30.hard_call.maf_mismatch\
  --score ~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/gp2_2025_prs_file.txt list-variants\
  --out ~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/terre_prs_gp2_2025
```

# DIG-PD PRS Analysis

### fam file set-up
```{r fam setup, eval=F}
# 1. Load the data
# check.names=FALSE is crucial so R doesn't alter your sample IDs with an "X"
traw <- read.table("/home1/NEURO/schaffner/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch.traw", header=TRUE, check.names=FALSE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
colnames(traw) <- sub("^(.*)_\\1$", "\\1", colnames(traw))

# Assuming your .pheno file has a header. 
# Update "your_data.pheno" to your actual file name
pheno <- read.table("/home1/NEURO/schaffner/SHARE_DECIPHER/pd_grs_ewas_integration/prs_analyses/DIGPD.pheno", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

# 2. Identify the overlapping samples
# Extract the sample IDs from the traw header (columns 7 to the end)
traw_samples <- colnames(traw)[7:ncol(traw)]
head(traw_samples) 


# Find the samples present in BOTH the traw file and your pheno file
# NOTE: Change 'pheno$IID' if your sample ID column is named differently
keep_samples <- intersect(traw_samples, pheno$IID)

# 3. Subset the .traw file
# Keep the first 6 metadata columns (CHR, SNP, etc.), plus the matching samples
traw_subset <- traw[, c(colnames(traw)[1:6], keep_samples)]

# 4. Generate the perfectly aligned .fam file data
# We build this directly from 'keep_samples' to guarantee perfect order
new_fam <- data.frame(
  FID = keep_samples,
  IID = keep_samples,
  Pat = 0,
  Mat = 0,
  Sex = 0,
  Pheno = -9 # Default to missing initially
)

# 5. Inject the phenotype data
# match() finds the correct row index in 'pheno' for each sample in 'new_fam',
# ensuring phenotypes are mapped without altering the row order.
# NOTE: Change 'pheno$Pheno_Value' to the actual name of your phenotype column
match_indices <- match(new_fam$IID, pheno$IID)
new_fam$Pheno <- pheno$PD[match_indices]

# add sex information
pheno_f <- read.table("/home1/NEURO/schaffner/SHARE_DECIPHER/pd_grs_ewas_integration/prs_analyses/DIGPD_female.pheno", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
pheno_m <- read.table("/home1/NEURO/schaffner/SHARE_DECIPHER/pd_grs_ewas_integration/prs_analyses/DIGPD_male.pheno", header=TRUE, stringsAsFactors=FALSE)
new_fam[new_fam$FID %in% pheno_f$FID,"Sex"] <- 2
new_fam[new_fam$FID %in% pheno_m$FID,"Sex"] <- 1

# 6. Export the new, clean files
write.table(new_fam, "/home1/NEURO/schaffner/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch_sub.fam", quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE, col.names=FALSE, sep="\t")
write.table(traw_subset, "/home1/NEURO/schaffner/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch_sub.traw", quote=FALSE, row.names=FALSE, col.names=TRUE, sep="\t")
```

Generate DIGPD PRS using `plink2 --score`:
```{bash eval=FALSE}
#removing header from traw file, was causing issues with plink 
tail -n +2 ~/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch_sub.traw > ~/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch_sub_noheader.traw

~/plink2 \
  --import-dosage ~/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch_sub_noheader.traw noheader skip0=1 skip1=2 chr-col-num=1 pos-col-num=4 ref-first \
  --fam ~/SHARE_DECIPHER/Genetic_data/DIGPD_Processed/raw_data.imputed.r2_90.maf_mismatch_sub.fam \
  --score ~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/gp2_2025_prs_file.txt list-variants \
  --out ~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/digpd_prs_gp2_2025

#Warning: --score: 37 entries in
#/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/gp2_2025_prs_file.txt
#were skipped due to missing variant IDs, and 1 was skipped due to a mismatching
#allele code.
#--score: 119 variants processed.
#--score: Variant list written to #/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/digpd_prs_gp2_2025.sscore.vars .
#--score: Results written to
#/home1/NEURO/schaffner/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/digpd_prs_gp2_2025.sscore

#119 variants/157 from GP2 passed QC in DIG-PD and were used to calculate the PRS.
```

# Plot the GP2 meta-analysis effect sizes for SNPs excluded from each sample
```{r gp2 beta, eval=F}
### TERRE
# Pre-compute jittered positions and add to dataframe
gp2_snps$jittered_x <- as.numeric(as.factor(gp2_snps$passed_TERRE_QC)) + 
                        runif(nrow(gp2_snps), -0.2, 0.2)
gp2_snps$jittered_y <- gp2_snps$Beta..all.studies

# Subset for labels
label_data <- gp2_snps[gp2_snps$Beta..all.studies > 0.5, ]

png("~/PD_GRS/WC_scripts/prs_analyses/gp2_snps_terre.png", width=300, height=300)
ggplot(gp2_snps, aes(x=passed_TERRE_QC, y=Beta..all.studies, col=passed_TERRE_QC)) + geom_boxplot(outlier.shape=NA) + geom_point(aes(x = jittered_x), stat = "identity")+ theme_classic() + ggtitle("GP2 GRS SNP weights in TERRE") + ylab("GP2 beta, all studies") + theme(legend.position="none") +
    geom_label_repel(
    data = label_data,
    aes(x = jittered_x, y = jittered_y, label = SNP),  # use pre-computed positions
    size = 3,
    force = 10,
    max.overlaps = 16,
    min.segment.length = 0.1
  )
dev.off()
```
